correctness.rationale: The indicated off-diagonal decay convention and one-end loss give the survival-time resolvent for P_1. Hilbert–Schmidt dissipation implies every imaginary-axis eigenoperator must have row and column 3 zero; the nearest-neighbor commutator in the eigenoperator equation then forces row and column 2, and then 1, zero. Thus the integral exists even at g=0. Independent exact elimination of the populations and a four-real-coherence solve reproduced the integrated density matrix with zero residual in the full equation and the trace N/D, including 87/14 at k=g=delta=1. The denominator is strictly positive. Exact expansion reproduced the first three derivative coefficients, both sign identities and coefficient positivity for degrees 3–8. Q_k grows strictly from a negative value to infinity. When Q_k<=0 all positive-degree derivative-numerator coefficients are positive, so equality at the threshold yields a zero endpoint slope but a strictly increasing curve thereafter. When Q_k>0 the signs change exactly once in coefficient order; by Descartes' rule and continuity there is one simple positive root and the slope changes from negative to positive. For x=|delta| the scaled leading polynomial at g=tx has its simple root at t=1, so the unique optimum approaches this branch. Exact next-order expansion then yields g_*=x-k/3+O(1/x), at fixed k. The independent threshold at k=1 is 0.189848784891488681 in detuning magnitude.
residual_risks: The large-detuning expansion is for each fixed k>0, not uniform as a trap rate varies with detuning. No numerical check was used to infer a global root count.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct result is the sharp all-k cubic threshold and sign-complete uniqueness classification for site-1 mean absorption in an exactly linear-gradient trimer with uniform site dephasing, including the -k/3 term. The compared papers supply related models/objectives and the compared catalogue statements supply exact neighboring trimer thresholds or optima, but none of the inspected statements implies this one. The closely relevant Haken–Strobl paper by Gaab and Bardeen remains a named access and equivalence risk, not a documented absence of coverage.
residual_risks: The Gaab–Bardeen full text was inaccessible. Neither a reciprocal mean-time equivalence there nor an unindexed identical theorem is excluded; no priority is inferred from catalogue dates.

checked_sources: Coates et al., arXiv:2106.12567 and arXiv:2210.11875
value.rationale: The result gives a global, all-parameter exclusion of multiple noise optima in a natural transport benchmark while identifying precisely when dephasing helps. It distinguishes endpoint preparation and mean survival from pumped throughput, and quantifies how trapping changes the large-gradient optimal noise scale. The exact threshold and uniqueness are useful beyond isolated parameter samples.
residual_risks: No claim of global uniqueness in other geometries or for other transport objectives follows.
